narrative_purpose: Teaches von Uexkull's core idea with his own example: the tick's entire perceivable world is three cues wide, and the roaring sensory abundance of the forest simply does not exist for it — the perceptual bubble made visible.
subject: A single tick waiting on the tip of a grass blade at the centre, enclosed in a faint translucent bubble; outside the bubble a richly detailed forest is rendered dim and grey and ignored; inside the bubble only three cues glow vividly — a rising warm scent plume from a mammal passing below, a soft radiant warmth, and a tactile suggestion of hair texture.
scene: A patch of forest floor and low grass, the unsensed forest receding into desaturated grey haze beyond the bubble.
camera: A close, slightly low macro view on the grass tip and tick, the bubble filling the frame, the grey forest as backdrop.
light: The three living cues glow as the only true light sources; everything outside the bubble is flat, dim and colourless to show it is filtered out.
palette: Vivid Pandora cyan and living teal plus a single warm amber scent-plume inside the bubble; muted desaturated grey-indigo outside it.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate with a faint diagrammatic clarity, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp on the tick and the three glowing cues; deliberately low-detail and grey on the ignored forest.
composition: Centred bubble with the tick at its heart, three cue-glows spaced around it, generous dim negative space outside for the contrast to land.
consistency_notes: Earth-science figure but rendered in the book's cool palette and from-within glow language so it sits beside the Pandoran plates; keep open dark space beside each cue for callout labels.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
